messages.content: You design reusable native parameter-update programs for existing scientific predictors. Return JSON keys design and source. source is Python using only host-supplied np (NumPy) and standard numeric/list/dict builtins. No imports, files, networking, torch, autograd, scipy, sklearn, optimization libraries or Markdown fences. You design the numerical mechanism; the researcher controls permissions, feedback validation and persistence. Do not request/infer real outcomes or original-method results. No new architecture or prediction wrapper. Public functions required: recipes(model), propose_linear(features, baseline, target, weights, recipe, shared), propose_rna(base_vector, hidden_directions, native_state, target, recipe).

Scientific objective: when a pretrained scientific predictor receives newly returned functional assays, improve its subsequent predictions by revising a bounded set of original model parameters. Construct one reusable program for the following native interfaces. You receive model equations and data schemas only, with no real arrays, scores, prior proposed algorithm, or query outcomes. Do not reproduce an assumed reference algorithm: design a sensible, computationally bounded, deterministic correction mechanism from the equations.

Linear native interfaces (function propose_linear): features has shape (n,G,D), target and baseline have shape (n,G). weights has shape (D,) when shared=True and shape (G,D) otherwise. For any newweights, native prediction exactly equals baseline + features@(newweights-weights), with the matrix product performed per output when shared=False. features includes native intercept coordinates, so arbitrary extra post-hoc output offsets are forbidden. baseline includes any immutable model offsets.
- model='scgpt': G=1024 selected RNA outputs, D=1026, shared=True. Actual output is c_g*(a_g@w_coeff+b_coeff)+(b_g@w_bias+b_bias), where c_g is known input control expression, a_g and b_g are fixed features from the pretrained coefficient/bias decoder branches. The feature coordinates are concatenated [c_g*a_g, c_g, b_g, 1]. The four native output tensors correspond exactly to these coordinates. Earlier encoders stay fixed; the shared last decoder hidden biases may additionally change through the native interface below. Target is log-normalized RNA expression after perturbation; baseline is the original native output. No candidate-specific RNA is an input.
- model='scfoundation': G=1024 selected RNA outputs, D=514, shared=False. Native GEARS integrated output is c_g + [own_g, context_1,...,context_512,1]@weights_g, where c_g is the known control input, own_g and context are computed by the original model and remain fixed. Each selected RNA has its own native coefficient row and intercept. These selected original native rows/intercepts are editable; the original normalization weights/bias and adjacent recovery hidden bias may additionally change through the native interface below. baseline includes c_g. Target is log-normalized RNA after perturbation. Consider computational cost: n is 8 per validation fit or 16 for final refit, while G and D are large. Do not create a (G*D)^2 matrix or full higher-dimensional pseudoinverse.

The RNA program is allowed the same final-readout and neighboring-hidden permission as the original framework. It may choose output-only edits or use hidden changes. Function propose_rna(base_vector, hidden_directions, native_state, target, recipe) returns a finite NEW native parameter vector of the same shape as base_vector. Its output coordinates are first, then permitted hidden coordinates. hidden_directions has shape (P,K), K<=32, with zeros in output coordinates and fixed directions in the permitted hidden coordinates; directions are host-supplied, generated independently of outcomes from the registered basis seed and native parameter scales. No query-specific data determine them. native_state(vector) is a host callback: it writes vector temporarily to the original model and runs ONLY the provided training-feedback identities, returning dict(features, baseline, weights, shared, output_width). Features/predictions/weights have exactly the linear schemas above at that vector's current hidden parameters. output_width is the initial segment containing native output parameters. For scGPT weights equals vector[:output_width] and shared=True. For scFoundation the output segment concatenates all G*513 coefficient values then G intercepts, so weights is their (G,514) assembled matrix and shared=False. To pack proposed per-RNA rows back into vector, concatenate newweights[:,:-1].reshape(-1) then newweights[:,-1]. For shared output use the returned vector directly. Hidden parameters are the remaining segment. You may call native_state to probe a bounded number of supplied hidden directions with finite differences and construct a deterministic regularized hidden update, then update native readout using the resulting state. Maximum calls per proposal=70, sufficient for two-sided probes of <=32 directions plus baseline/refit, and finite radius to keep hidden changes bounded. The callback gives you no held-feedback rows and no query features/outcomes. The host resets to base_vector after each proposal. Program may deliberately select output-only scope, but hidden permission is present. Every recipe model=scgpt/scfoundation is consumed by propose_rna; propose_linear is called directly only for Ridge and can also be used internally by propose_rna. You must define all four required functions.

recipes(model) returns deterministic JSON-serializable candidate dictionaries with unique string id, model and your numerical settings. Maximum candidate counts excluding original/no-op: scgpt 24 and scfoundation 32. Use a compact fixed menu within these limits. Functions must leave input arrays unchanged and return finite native values. Stabilized linear algebra and bounded finite-difference calculation allowed, no gradient descent/backpropagation or iterative optimization loops. You may choose readout-only or hidden/readout proposals; full permissions are present.

Researcher host: 16 feedback target genes, fixed 2-fold gene MSE validation, strict improvement over original/no-op followed by final refit. Each native_state call exposes only training-feedback rows, no held-feedback or query data. Three existing BASE seeds and three fixed target partitions are reused. Original checkpoints untouched. All predictions seal before query response evaluation. The host validates native parameter persistence/reload/reorder/singleton through the original model API. No query-dependent repair or proposal search.

Explain design: how native forward computation informs proposal; how measured discrepancies produce actual updates; regularization and bounds; generated-vs-host roles; why reuse fixed code across feedback. Return JSON design and source, with recipes, propose_linear, propose_rna. No original reference algorithm/results supplied.
